_full: FULL 5-clip COLOUR render — supersedes the walk pilot. Renders idle/walk/run/hurt/attack from the textured Meshy GLBs into the final thug_{action}.png set (overwrites the grey FBX sheets) + ONE rewritten thug_manifest.json. Reuses the proven pipeline: source=glb -> import_scene.gltf (keeps each GLB's PBR Material_1 + base-colour texture), the stray un-skinned 'Icosphere' is DROPped, the 4096² texture is downscaled to maxTextureSize (1024), view transform 'Standard' (true colour, not AgX), and inPlace root-strip removes locomotion TRAVEL on every clip (Z bob kept). Frame counts/fps/loop are IDENTICAL to the grey render (thug_gangster.json) so spriteManifest.test's locked cols (idle 6, walk 10, attack 8) stay green. Camera/framing/anchors/dirs are IDENTICAL too, so THUG_FACING_OFFSET (+4, #51) and the loader apply unchanged.
_sharedScale: ★ THE LOAD-BEARING ITEM. All 5 clips are in ONE job so the bbox pre-pass UNIONS their full frame ranges into ONE ortho_scale/figurePxH — every action renders at the SAME size (attack's wide arm-throw cannot shrink the normalised figure vs a compact idle). The render logs LOCKED-SCALE (the single scale + which clip/frame/dir drove the widest span + each clip's own extent) and asserts no clip escapes the shared union (RENDER_FAIL if it does). Do NOT render the clips as 5 separate jobs — that reintroduces per-clip scale.
_actions: idle/walk/run give the confirmed Meshy action names + source frame ranges. hurt (Gunshot_Reaction) and attack (Punch_Combo_4) intentionally OMIT actionName + frame range: each GLB is single-action, so the importer auto-selects its one action (no guessing) and the REAL action name flows into the manifest's sourceAction from action.name; the full clip range is used. If K's inspect shows either GLB is multi-action, add its exact actionName here.
_run: Windows PowerShell (SPLIT STREAMS; ErrorActionPreference Continue): $ErrorActionPreference='Continue'; & $env:BLENDER_PATH -b -P tools\blender\render_iso_unit.py -- --job tools\blender\render_jobs\thug_glb.json --engine BLENDER_EEVEE 1> thug_glb.out 2> thug_glb.err ; then paste thug_glb.out. THEN squeeze (K approved) — see README 'pngquant' block — and EYEBALL one squeezed sheet for banding before trusting 256 colours (photoreal gradients band harder than flat grey).

camera._note: IDENTICAL lock to the grey render (thug_gangster.json): 2:1 tiles -> dimetric2to1 (60deg from top-down). modelForwardDeg=0 like the grey render, so THUG_FACING_OFFSET=+4 (unitFacingQuantize.ts, #51) still applies. ⚠ FACING IS A K-GATE: the GLB imports via a DIFFERENT path than the FBX (import_scene.gltf, no automatic_bone_orientation), so its forward axis may differ. If the thug moonwalks (faces opposite travel) in-game, the fix is set THUG_FACING_OFFSET=0 (or re-render with modelForwardDeg:180).
